summary: Ethan Mollick argues that current AI models (GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1) already do weeks of human work when guided well, and that the real gap is a 'capability overhang' between what they can do and what people use them for. He gives hands-on examples, including GPT-6 Astra operating Blender and a browser-based video generator to make book trailers, and Fable 5.1 reconstructing Umberto Eco's library in 3D. He then pitches four human advantages (deep knowledge, wide knowledge, taste, agency) from his upcoming book Co-Existence, which has a pre-order bonus with a voice AI interview.
speakers_or_authors: Ethan Mollick (Wharton professor, One Useful Thing newsletter)
relevance_reason: The agent-operating-software passages (Blender, browser video generator, long unattended tasks) are directly relevant to computer-use agents, and he is a first-hand tester. The rest is general AI-and-work commentary and book promotion, with only a passing voice mention.

claims.claim: GPT-6 Astra operated Blender on its own, without clear instructions, building an animated 3D scene, script, voices, music and sound effects into a finished trailer in 45 minutes.
claims.quote: Without clear instructions from me, it proceeded to use Blender and build out an entire animated 3D scene (not an easy task), along with a script with some jokes and reveals

claims.claim: For a second trailer the AI used Blender output as a storyboard, drove a video generator through the author's browser, and edited the generated shots, with the author unaware of exactly how it did it.
claims.quote: it used the Blender animation as a storyboard, operated a video generator through my browser, and edited the generated shots into the final trailer.

claims.claim: Current models are barely used and poorly understood, so a large gap exists between what they can do and what people do with them.
claims.quote: the current capabilities of existing models are barely being used, and are often not even well understood.

claims.claim: The latest models can reliably do weeks of human work when properly guided and harnessed, enough for transformative economic impact.
claims.quote: they can reliably do weeks worth of human work when properly guided and harnessed.

claims.claim: Fable 5.1 reconstructed Umberto Eco's library in 3D from videos, photos and catalogues, placing about 5,000 identified books among 27,000 shelf slots and labelling each as certain, guess or unknown.
claims.quote: It marked every book certain, guess, or unknown, and drew the bookcases the cameras never reached in fog.

claims.claim: The author's own expertise was needed to catch AI errors and ask for revisions; the projects did not happen autonomously, and flaws remain.
claims.quote: I knew enough about Zork and Eco and my own book to see where the AI went wrong, and to ask for a second version when the first wasn't right.

claims.claim: Citing Anthropic work, experts get both better and more output from AI.
claims.quote: recent work from Anthropic suggests that expertise also shapes the quality of what AI gives back. Experts not only get better work out of AI, they get more work out of it.

claims.claim: Because making is now cheap, the scarce skill is selecting among outputs with taste, and the author's only decisions on the trailers were such choices.
claims.quote: Now making is fast and cheap. The scarce resource is your ability to select among stuff using your own taste.

claims.claim: Even if labs stopped training new models, existing ones would still change how large parts of the economy work.
claims.quote: If every lab stopped training new models tomorrow, that wouldn’t change the fact that GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 are already enough to change how large parts of the economy work.

commercial_interest: The author is promoting his book Co-Existence (out October 20) and offers a pre-order bonus, a free voice interview with an AI that reports on the reader's four advantages. The post also praises products he uses and pays for (ChatGPT account), and the examples are self-reported with no independent test.
older_event: No. The post discusses recent model releases (GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1) and the author's new experiments; no older event dominates.
